text:
Evelyn Tran: hey! first day, using Windows with WSL2 + VS Code devcontainer. followed quickstart but asdf versions differ between host WSL and the container. where do you recommend installing asdf and runtime versions? :wave:
DevX Bot: welcome Evelyn! quick rule: if you do most work inside the devcontainer, install asdf and languages inside the container. If you use host terminals a lot, install in WSL user. paste `cat .devcontainer/Dockerfile` and `cat .tool-versions` if you want specific advice.
Evelyn Tran: .devcontainer/Dockerfile copies the repo but doesn't install asdf. .tool-versions lists python 3.11.4 and nodejs 18.16.0. right now container python is 3.10 and host (WSL) is 3.11.
Marcus: easiest fix: add an asdf bootstrap step to the devcontainer Dockerfile or postCreateCommand in devcontainer.json. Example postCreateCommand: `bash -lc "git clone https://github.com/asdf-vm/asdf.git ~/.asdf --branch v0.12.0 && . ~/.asdf/asdf.sh && asdf plugin-add python && asdf install"`
Samir: alternative is volume-mounting your ~/.asdf into the container, but that can create permission/path mismatches. We prefer installing inside the container to keep builds reproducible. Also ensure you run `asdf reshim` after installs.
Priya: note that direnv and 1password session tokens are per-environment. If your repo relies on OP_SESSION_* via direnv, sign into 1password inside the container (`eval $(op signin --raw my)`) or use the 1password extension for devcontainers. Otherwise direnv will deny .envrc.
Evelyn Tran: added the postCreateCommand and re-opened in container. asdf shims now present but VS Code terminals still show system python in the container.
Marcus: check the PATH ordering in the container shell rc (we use bash in our container examples). Put `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"` early in /etc/profile or ~/.bashrc and source asdf: `. $HOME/.asdf/asdf.sh`. Then reopen the integrated terminal. Also run `asdf which python` to confirm shim target.
Evelyn Tran: `asdf which python` points to ~/.asdf/installs/python/3.11.4/bin/python, `python --version` now 3.11.4 inside container. great. last Q: how to get company dotfiles/hook setup in container?
Samir: clone our dotfiles during container build or as part of postCreateCommand: `git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/dotfiles ~/dotfiles && ~/dotfiles/setup.sh`. If your setup requires OP_SESSION, run signin interactively after the container starts. The setup script will install pre-commit hooks and symlink config files into the container home.
Evelyn Tran: cloning + setup ran fine after signing in to 1password inside container. thanks everyone, tagging @Marcus if I hit more devcontainer quirks. excited to be here! :tada:
